security_audit.summary: Most static matches are scanner false positives caused by JavaScript regular-expression methods, Markdown code formatting, fixed sibling references, and documented local tooling. A material workflow risk remains: the skill instructs agents to silently fetch and apply remote HyperFrames skill updates before use, allowing reviewed content to change without consent. Static review was capped at 400/822 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 422 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The workflow silently updates remote skill content before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update step. Present the version and changelog, then require explicit user approval before downloading or applying updates.

remediation.issue: The workflow invokes external GitHub and media tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before network operations and state which PR data, avatars, and media-provider requests will be sent.

remediation.issue: Project paths may be explicitly supplied by a caller.
remediation.suggestion: Document the allowed output directory and enforce a configurable allowlist when operating in managed environments.

content.user_title: Turn a Pull Request into a Video
content.value_statement: Pull requests can be difficult to explain to teammates and stakeholders. This skill turns verified PR facts into a structured HyperFrames explainer video.
actual_capabilities: Fetches pull request metadata, changed files, commits, and diffs through the GitHub CLI.
Creates a PR-specific project directory outside the caller repository by default.
Builds a storyboard and narration plan from real pull request evidence.
Generates frame compositions, captions, transitions, and a final MP4 through HyperFrames.
Downloads contributor avatars for an optional credits frame.
Validates video output with HyperFrames lint, check, and snapshots.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication and access to the target pull request.
Requires HyperFrames and optional media providers for full rendering and audio features.
Does not capture a product interface or create a marketing video from a website.
The final render requires user approval after the review checkpoint.

use_cases.title: Explain a release change
use_cases.description: Turn a merged pull request into a concise release walkthrough with verified code examples.

use_cases.title: Prepare a code review recap
use_cases.description: Create a visual summary of a complex pull request for reviewers and project leads.

use_cases.title: Share a refactor update
use_cases.description: Present the purpose and effect of a refactor without reading the full diff aloud.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PR video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short explainer video for GitHub PR owner/repo#123. Summarize the main change and ask for approval before rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a bug fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this PR into a bug-fix walkthrough. Focus on the problem, the changed code, and the user impact: https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123.

prompt_templates.title: Create a release recap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release-ready PR video for owner/repo#123. Use a clear changelog structure, include two real diff excerpts, and use a calm narration voice.

prompt_templates.title: Create a silent technical walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a silent visual walkthrough for owner/repo#123. Do not generate narration or music. Use captions and code-focused frames, then pause for review before rendering.

output_examples.input: Explain PR owner/repo#123 as a bug-fix video.
output: A project folder with captured PR facts and extracted diff evidence.
A storyboard that explains the bug, the fix, and the expected impact.
A review-ready video preview and final MP4 after approval.

output_examples.input: Create a silent refactor walkthrough from a pull request URL.
output: A code-focused storyboard with no narration or background music.
Frame compositions, captions, validation results, and a rendered video after review.

best_practices: Use a pull request URL or owner/repository number that you can access with GitHub CLI.
Review the storyboard and real diff excerpts before approving a render.
Use a dedicated project directory for generated assets and video output.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for website captures or product marketing videos without a pull request.
Do not approve a render before checking the storyboard, snapshots, and validation results.
Do not assume missing GitHub permissions can be bypassed; authenticate and request access instead.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a GitHub pull request URL, an owner/repository number, or a current repository pull request.

faq.question: Does it capture a website interface?
faq.answer: No. It creates an explainer from pull request metadata, commits, files, and diff content.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub CLI must be authenticated and authorized to read the pull request.

faq.question: Can it work with private pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes, when the authenticated GitHub account has access to the repository and pull request.

faq.question: Can I create a video without narration?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the silent workflow option to skip narration and background music.

faq.question: When is the final video rendered?
faq.answer: The skill renders after validation and the required user review approval.
